scenes.narration: At this point in your career, most meaningful opportunities don't come from job boards.

vars.title: Finding New Peers, Sponsors, and Opportunity Holders

scenes.narration: They come from people—colleagues, leaders, and connectors who know your work and can open doors.
In this module, we'll focus on three kinds of relationships that matter especially during a mid-career pivot or advancement: peers, sponsors, and opportunity holders.
Peers are professionals at a similar level who share knowledge, introductions, and real-world context.
They help you understand what's happening on the ground, compare experiences, and build community as you shift direction.

vars.label: What peers do
vars.heading: Ground Truth and Community
vars.point1: Understand what's happening on the ground
vars.point3: Build community as you shift direction

pointCues: understand what's happening on the ground

scenes.narration: Think of colleagues in your department, practitioners in your future field, and members of the professional communities you belong to.

vars.label: Think of
vars.heading: Where to Find Peers
vars.chips: Colleagues in your department,Practitioners in your future field,Professional communities you belong to

scenes.narration: Sponsors are more senior leaders who don't just advise you—they actively advocate for you.
They put your name forward for roles, projects, and committees.
Sponsorship is especially critical for mid-career advancement and career pivots, because sponsors often sit right where decisions get made—the promotions, the project leads, the committee seats.

vars.label: Why it's critical
vars.heading: Sponsors Sit Where Decisions Get Made
vars.chips: The promotions,The project leads,The committee seats

scenes.narration: Opportunity holders are people who control or influence roles, projects, and hiring decisions.
This might be hiring managers, program directors, deans, HR or talent partners, or leaders in organizations you'd like to join.

vars.label: Who counts
vars.heading: Many Faces, One Role
vars.point4: Leaders in organizations you'd like to join

scenes.narration: Even if they don't know you yet, they are key nodes for your future path.

vars.statement: They Are Key Nodes for Your Path

scenes.narration: When you're pivoting into a new field or aiming for a higher-level role, your goal is not to meet everyone. Your goal is to identify a small, strategic map of the people who are most relevant to the future you're building.

vars.bSub: The people most relevant to your future

scenes.narration: So how do you find these people? First, start with your existing connections: Current and former colleagues, People you've worked with on cross-functional projects, Alumni networks, professional associations, or communities you're part of

vars.label: Method one
vars.heading: Start with Existing Connections
vars.point2: People you've worked with on cross-functional projects
vars.point3: Alumni networks, professional associations, or communities you're part of

scenes.narration: Let them know about your Next Move Statement and ask: "Who do you know in my target field or role that I might talk to for a twenty-minute learning conversation?"

Second, use platforms like LinkedIn and professional groups to search directly in your future field: Search by title, skills, or keywords connected to your target roles, Look for people in organizations or teams you'd like to join

vars.label: Method two
vars.heading: Search Your Future Field Directly
vars.point1: Search by title, skills, or keywords for your target roles
vars.point2: Look for people in organizations or teams you'd like to join

scenes.narration: Third, identify potential sponsors in your current organization or a new one: People one to three levels above you who appreciate your work or seem aligned with your direction, Leaders who are visible in the spaces you want to enter

vars.label: Method three
vars.heading: Identify Potential Sponsors
vars.point1: People one to three levels above you
vars.point2: Leaders visible in the spaces you want to enter

pointCues: one to three levels above you

scenes.narration: In this module's activity, you'll build a contact map of three to five strategic relationships—peers, sponsors, and opportunity holders—who are relevant to your next move, then use outreach templates and AI to craft authentic messages.

vars.context: Peers, sponsors, and opportunity holders who are relevant to your next move.

scenes.narration: Remember: networking is not about collecting business cards or asking for favors at random.
It's about building real relationships, sharing value, and staying visible to the people who are most connected to the future you're creating.

vars.lines: Sharing value|Staying visible to the right people

scenes.narration: As you move forward, ask yourself: "Who already sits near the opportunities I care about—and how can I begin a genuine, respectful relationship with them?"

vars.next: Who already sits near the opportunities you care about?
